newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Dalgety long-term rating to A minus.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Dalgety long-term rating to A minus.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 18 - IBCA, the European credit rating agency, issued the following statement on Wednesday.
IBCA has lowered its long-term rating for Dalgety plc from A to A minus. The A1 short-term rating is affirmed.

Dalgety is Europe's second largest petfood manufacturer, one of the largest European food ingredients suppliers, the leading UK agribusiness for the supply of animal feed and agrochemicals and the world's largest hybrid pig breeder.

Dalgety's results for FY96 were adversely affected by the costs of integrating the Quaker European Pet Foods (QEPF) acquisition, combined with the impact of BSE on its European operations. The EU imposed ban on the export of any UK beef products temporarily halted sales of UK manufactured petfoods to Continental Europe and some existing stocks had to be written off.

BSE also reduced demand for the processed foods that are a major market for Dalgety Food Ingredients and Dalgety's agribusiness suffered from lower demand for feedstuffs, the writing off of stocks containing meat or bonemeal and from the need to reformulate products with more expensive soya protein.

The QEPF acquisition was a good long-term strategic move to lessen Dalgety's dependence on cyclical businesses, but the full benefits from the integration have been delayed by BSE, which will continue to affect the company for at least the first half of FY97.

Financial risk has increased as a result of the debt incurred in the QEPF purchase. Although debt has reduced as planned through disposals, Dalgety is more vulnerable to events beyond its control. While dividends are expected to be covered in FY97, IBCA sees little scope to reduce gearing levels through retained earnings until the petfoods business can improve its performance and other trading conditions return to normality.
